arrival_summary: Earliest reachable bin endpoint minus window start, including initial waiting; statistics condition on reachable ordered pairs and are not observed continuous latencies.

budgets.over_budget: fail before graph allocation; no sampling, actor dropping or solver substitution

denominator: Ordered distinct-actor pairs: n*(n-1)=12656 for n=113. Static unordered reachable counts must be doubled before count comparison.
graph_encoding: Sparse actor/bin before-after states plus source/sink states; contacts cross before-to-after; waits move within and between actor states; nonstrict adds same-bin after-to-before arcs.
inclusion_checks: strict reachable pair set is a subset of nonstrict
nonstrict reachable pair set is a subset of same-window same-threshold static pairs
nonstrict earliest endpoint never exceeds strict for each shared reachable pair
measurement: Both variants are conventions applied to archived bin labels; no contact duration, continuous transfer time, relay probability or actual transmission is identified.
node_universe: All 113 endpoint IDs observed anywhere in the reviewed archive, retained in every graph; retrospective and not an independently verified attendance roster.
nonstrict: Contact-bin endpoints may be equal; allow arbitrary relay within a same-bin contact component.
not_in_scope: real-world lower or upper transmission bounds
pair_filter: Apply the whole-window cumulative bin count first, then retain all in-window records of qualifying pairs. Three bins need not be consecutive. For threshold >1, early admissibility uses later records in that same window.
path_engine: Original NetworkX 3.7 single_source_shortest_path_length; use reachable state keys, never interpret BFS edge-count distances as elapsed seconds.

primary_references.title: Connectivity and Inference Problems for Temporal Networks
The Complexity of Finding Small Separators in Temporal Graphs

research_question: How much ordered-pair reachability in the reviewed static recorded-contact graphs remains when contact-bin order is respected, and how sensitive is it to same-bin relay assumptions?
source_assumption: Analyze each actor separately with a hypothetical signal available at the window start; this is not a joint multi-source broadcast observation.
strict: Successive contact-bin endpoints must strictly increase; at most one contact hop in a bin.
validation_plan: Synthetic order/bin/boundary/waiting/denominator/censoring counterexamples with real upstream paths; actual reviewed-source CLI; independent raw-TSV parser and different sparse actor/time graph encoding using original NetworkX; existing native regression tests.
waiting_assumption: Unlimited lossless waiting within the window, including gaps with no recorded contacts. No attendance, sensor uptime or actual signal retention is inferred.
